subject: Maths
question: Find the least 5-digit number which when divided by 20, 22 and 36 leaves a remainder of 3 in each case.
solution: LCM(20, 22, 36) = 1980. The least 5-digit number is 10000; 10000 ÷ 1980 leaves 100, so the least multiple of 1980 that is 5 digits long is 10000 + (1980 − 100) = 11880. 11880 + 3 = 11883. The answer is 11883.
questionHi: पाँच अंकों की वह सबसे छोटी संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए जो 20, 22 और 36 से भाग देने पर प्रत्येक दशा में 3 शेष छोड़ती है।

subject: Maths
question: Three numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and their LCM is 1620. What is their HCF?
solution: The numbers are 3k, 4k, 5k, so their HCF is k and their LCM is k × LCM(3, 4, 5) = 60k. 60k = 1620 gives k = 27. The HCF is 27 (numbers 81, 108, 135).
questionHi: तीन संख्याएँ 3 : 4 : 5 के अनुपात में हैं और उनका LCM 1620 है। उनका HCF क्या है?

subject: Maths
question: Four lights flash at intervals of 6, 7, 15 and 50 seconds respectively. If they flash together now, after how many seconds will they next flash together?
solution: They are together again after a time that is a multiple of every interval - the least is the LCM. 6 = 2 × 3, 7 = 7, 15 = 3 × 5, 50 = 2 × 5², so LCM(6, 7, 15, 50) = 1050 seconds.
questionHi: चार बत्तियाँ क्रमशः 6, 7, 15 और 50 सेकंड के अंतराल पर चमकती हैं। यदि वे अभी एक साथ चमकती हैं, तो कितने सेकंड बाद वे फिर एक साथ चमकेंगी?
solutionHi: वे फिर उस समय साथ होंगी जो हर अंतराल का गुणज हो - सबसे कम LCM है। 6 = 2 × 3, 7 = 7, 15 = 3 × 5, 50 = 2 × 5², अतः LCM(6, 7, 15, 50) = 1050 सेकंड।

question: What is the least number, other than 1, which when divided by 6, 10, 11 and 25 leaves a remainder of 1 in each case?
solution: A number leaving remainder 1 with each is (a common multiple) + 1. LCM(6, 10, 11, 25) = 1650, so the least such number after 1 is 1650 + 1 = 1651.
questionHi: 1 को छोड़कर वह सबसे छोटी संख्या कौन-सी है जिसे 6, 10, 11 और 25 से भाग देने पर प्रत्येक दशा में 1 शेष बचता है?

question: Two numbers are in the ratio 7 : 13 and their LCM is 1365. What is their HCF?
solution: The numbers are 7k and 13k; 7 and 13 are co-prime, so HCF = k and LCM = 7 × 13 × k = 91k. 91k = 1365 gives k = 15. The HCF is 15 (numbers 105 and 195).
questionHi: दो संख्याएँ 7 : 13 के अनुपात में हैं और उनका LCM 1365 है। उनका HCF क्या है?
solutionHi: संख्याएँ 7k और 13k हैं; 7 और 13 सह-अभाज्य हैं, अतः HCF = k और LCM = 7 × 13 × k = 91k। 91k = 1365 से k = 15। HCF = 15 (संख्याएँ 105 और 195)।

question: The HCF of two numbers is 39 and their LCM is 12870. If one of the numbers is 585, what is the other?

question: Bricks measuring 28 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm are stacked to make a solid cube. What is the least number of bricks needed?
solution: The side of the cube must be a multiple of each edge: the least is LCM(28, 6, 4) = 84 cm. Bricks = (84 ÷ 28) × (84 ÷ 6) × (84 ÷ 4) = 3 × 14 × 21 = 882.

question: The traffic lights at three crossings change every 25, 34 and 85 seconds respectively. If they all change together at 7:00:00 AM, at what time will they next change together?
solution: LCM(25, 34, 85) = 850 seconds = 14 minutes 10 seconds. 7:00:00 AM + 14 minutes 10 seconds = 7:14:10 AM.

question: 216 guava, 324 lemon and 351 neem trees are to be planted in rows, with the same number of trees in every row and only one kind of tree in a row. What is the least number of rows needed?
solution: Fewest rows means the most trees in a row: HCF(216, 324, 351) = 27. Rows = 216 ÷ 27 + 324 ÷ 27 + 351 ÷ 27 = 8 + 12 + 13 = 33.
questionHi: 216 अमरूद, 324 नींबू और 351 नीम के पेड़ पंक्तियों में लगाने हैं: हर पंक्ति में पेड़ों की संख्या समान हो और एक पंक्ति में एक ही प्रकार के पेड़ हों। कम से कम कितनी पंक्तियाँ चाहिए?

question: What is the least number that must be subtracted from 66971 so that the result is exactly divisible by 18, 27 and 32?
solution: A number divisible by 18, 27 and 32 is a multiple of their LCM, 864. 66971 ÷ 864 leaves 443, so take away 443 to reach 66528.
questionHi: 66971 में से कम से कम कौन-सी संख्या घटाई जाए कि शेष 18, 27 और 32 से पूरी तरह विभाज्य हो जाए?
solutionHi: 18, 27 और 32 से विभाज्य संख्या उनके LCM 864 की गुणज है। 66971 ÷ 864 का शेषफल 443, अतः 443 घटाने पर 66528।

subject: Maths
question: Find the greatest 4-digit number which is exactly divisible by 4, 5 and 21.
solution: LCM(4, 5, 21) = 420. The greatest 4-digit number is 9999; 9999 ÷ 420 leaves 339, so the greatest multiple of 420 is 9999 − 339 = 9660. The answer is 9660.
questionHi: चार अंकों की वह सबसे बड़ी संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए जो 4, 5 और 21 से पूरी तरह विभाज्य है।

question: The LCM of two numbers is 14 times their HCF, and the sum of the HCF and the LCM is 570. If one of the numbers is 76, what is the other?
solution: HCF + 14 × HCF = 570, so 15 × HCF = 570 and HCF = 38; LCM = 14 × 38 = 532. Other number = HCF × LCM ÷ 76 = 38 × 532 ÷ 76 = 266.
questionHi: दो संख्याओं का LCM उनके HCF का 14 गुना है, और HCF तथा LCM का योग 570 है। यदि एक संख्या 76 है, तो दूसरी संख्या क्या है?

subject: Maths
question: Find the least 4-digit number which is exactly divisible by 6, 10 and 32.
solution: LCM(6, 10, 32) = 480. The least 4-digit number is 1000; 1000 ÷ 480 leaves 40, so the least multiple of 480 that is 4 digits long is 1000 + (480 − 40) = 1440. The answer is 1440.
questionHi: चार अंकों की वह सबसे छोटी संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए जो 6, 10 और 32 से पूरी तरह विभाज्य है।

subject: Maths
question: A shopkeeper has 92 litres, 368 litres and 414 litres of three kinds of oil. He fills them, without mixing, into tins of one size so that every tin is full. What is the least number of tins he needs?
solution: Fewest tins means the biggest tin: HCF(92, 368, 414) = 46 litres. Tins = 92 ÷ 46 + 368 ÷ 46 + 414 ÷ 46 = 2 + 8 + 9 = 19.
questionHi: एक दुकानदार के पास तीन प्रकार का तेल क्रमशः 92 लीटर, 368 लीटर और 414 लीटर है। वह इन्हें बिना मिलाए एक ही आकार के डिब्बों में भरता है ताकि हर डिब्बा पूरा भरा हो। उसे कम से कम कितने डिब्बे चाहिए?

question: In an exam 40 students take Hindi, 120 take English and 340 take Maths. Every room must seat the same number of students, all taking the same subject. What is the least number of rooms needed?

question: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 1, is exactly divisible by 12, 30, 35 and 40?
solution: The number + 1 must be a common multiple; the least is LCM(12, 30, 35, 40) = 840. So the number is 840 − 1 = 839.

subject: Maths
question: Four runners go round a circular track in 12, 66, 90 and 99 seconds respectively. If they start together from the same point, after how many seconds will they all be at the starting point together again?
solution: Each is back at the start after a whole number of rounds, i.e. at a multiple of his round time; all together first at LCM(12, 66, 90, 99) = 1980 seconds (33 minutes).
questionHi: चार धावक एक वृत्ताकार पथ का एक चक्कर क्रमशः 12, 66, 90 और 99 सेकंड में लगाते हैं। यदि वे एक ही बिंदु से एक साथ दौड़ना शुरू करें, तो कितने सेकंड बाद वे सब फिर आरंभ-बिंदु पर एक साथ होंगे?

question: Find the HCF of 540, 1350 and 3600.
solution: 540 = 2² × 3³ × 5, 1350 = 2 × 3³ × 5², 3600 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5². Only the primes common to all 3 numbers count, each with its lowest power: 2 × 3² × 5 = 90. (540 and 1350 alone have HCF 270, but 3600 does not share all of it.)

question: Find the greatest number that divides 2466, 2739 and 2921, leaving the same remainder in each case.

question: Find the greatest 4-digit number which when divided by 25, 30 and 39 leaves a remainder of 4 in each case.

question: What is the greatest number that divides 207, 975 and 1023, leaving a remainder of 15 in each case?

question: 46 pencils, 92 erasers and 207 notebooks are to be shared among the greatest possible number of children so that each child gets the same number of each item, with nothing left over. How many notebooks does each child get?

question: Three people walk with steps of 34 cm, 44 cm and 85 cm respectively. What is the least distance each of them can cover in a whole number of steps?

question: What is the LCM of 21, 24, 26 and 27?
solution: 21 = 3 × 7, 24 = 2³ × 3, 26 = 2 × 13, 27 = 3³. Take every prime with its highest power: 2³ × 3³ × 7 × 13 = 19656. So the LCM is 19656.

solution: They are together again after a time that is a multiple of every interval - the least is the LCM. 12 = 2² × 3, 30 = 2 × 3 × 5, 39 = 3 × 13, 40 = 2³ × 5, so LCM(12, 30, 39, 40) = 1560 seconds.

question: A shopkeeper has 100 litres, 200 litres and 325 litres of three kinds of milk. He fills them, without mixing, into tins of one size so that every tin is full. What is the least number of tins he needs?
solution: Fewest tins means the biggest tin: HCF(100, 200, 325) = 25 litres. Tins = 100 ÷ 25 + 200 ÷ 25 + 325 ÷ 25 = 4 + 8 + 13 = 25.

question: A sweet seller packs his laddoos in boxes of 8, 12 and 13. Whichever box size he uses, at least one box is filled and 4 laddoos are left over. What is the least number of laddoos he can have?
solution: Leaving 4 each time means (the number − 4) divides by each box size; with a box filled it is not 0, so it is at least LCM(8, 12, 13) = 312. Least number = 312 + 4 = 316.
questionHi: एक मिठाई वाला अपने लड्डू 8, 12 और 13 के डिब्बों में पैक करता है। वह कोई भी डिब्बा-आकार ले, कम से कम एक डिब्बा भरता है और 4 लड्डू बच जाते हैं। उसके पास कम से कम कितने लड्डू हैं?

solution: Write them in hundredths: 9, 16, 32. LCM(9, 16, 32) = 288, so the LCM is 288 hundredths = 2.88.

question: What is the least common multiple of 232 and 870?
solution: 232 = 2³ × 29, 870 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 29. Every prime that appears, each with its highest power: 2³ × 3 × 5 × 29 = 3480. So the LCM is 3480.

question: What is the least number that must be added to 80439 so that the sum is exactly divisible by 9, 12 and 20?
solution: A number divisible by 9, 12 and 20 is a multiple of their LCM, 180. 80439 ÷ 180 leaves 159, so add 180 − 159 = 21 to reach 80460.

question: Find the least number which when divided by 16, 22 and 28 leaves remainders 12, 18 and 24 respectively.
solution: Each remainder is 4 less than its divisor: 16 − 12 = 4, 22 − 18 = 4, 28 − 24 = 4. So the number + 4 is divisible by all of them: the least is LCM(16, 22, 28) − 4 = 1232 − 4 = 1228.

question: Find the greatest 4-digit number which is exactly divisible by 8, 12 and 33.
solution: LCM(8, 12, 33) = 264. The greatest 4-digit number is 9999; 9999 ÷ 264 leaves 231, so the greatest multiple of 264 is 9999 − 231 = 9768. The answer is 9768.

question: Find the HCF of 5/16, 15/14 and 25/4.
solution: HCF of fractions = HCF of the numerators ÷ LCM of the denominators = HCF(5, 15, 25) ÷ LCM(16, 14, 4) = 5/112.

question: What is the least number, other than 6, which when divided by 7, 10, 15 and 27 leaves a remainder of 6 in each case?
solution: A number leaving remainder 6 with each is (a common multiple) + 6. LCM(7, 10, 15, 27) = 1890, so the least such number after 6 is 1890 + 6 = 1896.

question: What is the least perfect square that is exactly divisible by each of 21, 28 and 30?
solution: LCM(21, 28, 30) = 420 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7. For a square every power must be even, so multiply by 3 × 5 × 7: 420 × 105 = 44100 = 210².

question: 44 mango, 132 guava and 330 lemon trees are to be planted in rows, with the same number of trees in every row and only one kind of tree in a row. What is the least number of rows needed?
solution: Fewest rows means the most trees in a row: HCF(44, 132, 330) = 22. Rows = 44 ÷ 22 + 132 ÷ 22 + 330 ÷ 22 = 2 + 6 + 15 = 23.

question: What is the greatest number that divides 215, 509 and 551, leaving a remainder of 5 in each case?
solution: Take off the remainder: 215 − 5 = 210, 509 − 5 = 504, 551 − 5 = 546. The number must divide all of these exactly: HCF(210, 504, 546) = 42, and 42 is more than 5, so the answer is 42.

question: Three numbers are in the ratio 4 : 6 : 9 and their LCM is 1440. What is their HCF?
solution: The numbers are 4k, 6k, 9k, so their HCF is k and their LCM is k × LCM(4, 6, 9) = 36k. 36k = 1440 gives k = 40. The HCF is 40 (numbers 160, 240, 360).
